current.text: He joined Boston in the Jaylen Brown trade.
He is the clear number two option in Boston behind Jayson Tatum, after being the third option in Philadelphia.
He is a projected starter at forward next to Derrick White and Jayson Tatum.
Experts expect more usage and minutes in Boston, with usage near 26 after 23 last season and about 32 minutes.
He enters the season healthy, with no surgery this offseason and fully rested.
Last season he came in off knee surgery, and 25 of his missed games came from a PED suspension.
Experts think availability fears are overdone and see a high chance he plays clearly more games than last season, though missed games remain a risk.
Boston has 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league, and three of them fall in our playoff window.
He is expected to sit some back-to-backs, maybe 8 to 10, but not all of them.
Boston plays 4-3-4 games in weeks 19 to 21 with a March 28 end, one game short of the maximum.
Experts project him as a top 40 per game player with top 30 upside, and some see an outside shot at the top 25 or top 20.
His ceiling depends on games and efficiency: top 40 to top 30 if he reaches about 60 to 65 games, and top 40 if his rim finishing bounces back from 57% toward 63% with one or two more shots per game.
Experts call his ADP of about 75 to 80 too low and would happily draft him in the 60s or rounds 6 to 7. There is little risk at his price.
In an auction mock he went for 15 USD, which Josh called very good value. Josh would have paid up to 20 USD.
Avoid stacking him with too many other older, injury-prone players.
One expert thinks he will probably not stay in Boston long, and this may be his only season there.

durable.text: Steals are his best category. He also makes threes in volume and shoots free throws well.
His FG% is a weak spot, a mild drag on a team's FG%.
His game is fantasy friendly and broad. He adds scoring, threes, rebounds, assists and steals and is more than a 3-and-D player.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues.
He is an adaptable player who can scale his usage up or down.
He has a long injury history, with recurring knee problems for years plus UCL and shoulder issues.
He served a 25-game PED suspension in 2025-26.

note: Experts agree he is underpriced. Yahoo values him at 12 USD but his average cost is only 2.4 USD (ESPN 3 USD), he went for 9 USD in our league last season, and a recent auction mock sold him for 15 USD with Josh willing to go to 20 USD. Paying in the low to mid teens fits builds that want steals, threes and FT% from a forward and can absorb a small FG% drag. Early in the season, check how many of Boston's 16 back-to-backs he sits, whether his usage really rises as the number two option, and whether his knees hold up.
